seeds.text: Runtime truth belongs in seglog/redb/projections per newer guidance (GPT-5.4 sweep).
Primary schemas stop at node-level modeling; they cannot represent work package, feature seam, lane, promotion class, contamination state, resolution thread, or effective account identity.
Acceptance, evidence, coverage, GUI automation, and test schemas represent nodes/checks but not the package/seam/lane/account object family.

Storage/event keys remain thin: many contracts have run_id/node_id but lack project_id, attempt_id, package_id, seam_id, lane_id, worktree_id, safe_point_id, promotion_class, and requested/effective account fields.
Multi-account is surfaced in UX before it is modeled canonically in runtime/storage/schema contracts.
Provider/persona docs still encode old orchestration ownership (phase/task/subtask/iteration, singular Overseer) despite runtime records already carrying node_id and attempt_id.
Fallback behavior is contradictory across core docs (persona fallback split; GitHub vs multi-account; Docker/media stopping at provider/model).
GitHub auth retry rules conflict with multi-account failover expectations.
Docker/media/provider flows usually stop at provider/model, not account-resolution lineage.
Settings scopes are too coarse: global/project toggles dominate; package/seam/lane/run/account-aware policy scopes are mostly absent.
Package-based lane pools are still missing as a canonical concept while SCM docs assume subtask worktrees, branch-per-run, and direct merge/PR patterns.

Worktree visibility is only partially wired between Source Control and Orchestrator (status stops at repo/worktree/branch/tier, not package/lane ownership, contamination, restore eligibility, promotion posture).
Parallelism is modeled in outdated shapes (per-thread queues, per-provider caps, parallel subtasks, crews per tier) that do not map to package/seam promotion or lane-pool capacity.

Contamination policy is a vocabulary gap: safe-point language exists in addenda but contamination classification, restore-before-reuse, and lane quarantine semantics are absent from main SCM/worktree contracts.
Priority 1 cleanup targets canonical contracts that cannot coexist with the new model (Orchestrator_Page, Executor_Protocol, Contracts_V0, storage-plan, human-in-the-loop, plan graph schemas).
Priority 2 addresses misleading UI/SCM/operator docs (FinalGUISpec, Run_Graph_View, WorktreeGitImprovement, GitHub_Integration, Widget_System, UI_Command_Catalog).
Priority 3 covers terminology, routing, and anti-drift docs (00-plans-index, Crosswalk, Glossary, feature-list, OpenCode_Coverage_Matrix, Project_Output_Artifacts).

Single Overseer vs package + seam overseer models leave scheduling/review/recovery/promotion ownership ambiguous if both persist.

Extend requested/effective runtime identity to account and overseer role; effective account switching remains mostly unmodeled.
Choose one HITL model and one action family (tier-boundary approvals, graph-local commands, and blocked-node runtime actions currently compete).
Separate plan structure from mutable runtime state; runtime truth is split across plan shards, JSON sidecars, and event/projection docs.
Specify package-based worktree lane pools end-to-end—no single canonical lane-pool model exists yet.
Orchestrator_Page remains a primary runtime owner for orchestration UX but still encodes Tiers, Phase/Task/Subtask, singular Overseer, and legacy persona_id fields.
Executor_Protocol still encodes singular scheduler authority and lexicographic-style selection language.
human-in-the-loop.md and Project_Output_Artifacts.md still define tier-boundary HITL, legacy workspace paths, and lingering allowed_actions[] usage.
plan_graph and project_plan_graph_index schemas assume node-only lifecycle and lexicographic selection without blocked/contaminated/restore-required states.

GUI rebuild surfaces (Orchestrator_Page, Run_Graph_View, Widget_System, GUI_Rebuild_Requirements_Checklist) must replace tier-primary mental model with package/seam/lane/promotion/contamination/resolution-thread UX.
Attention routing should be explicit Dashboard → Orchestrator → chat-thread for blocked and major-decision paths (not only thread-local/wizard-local).
Contracts_V0 vs Orchestrator_Page: canonical persona naming disagrees before account identity is fully added; account fallback fields missing.
allowed_actions[] vs allowed_action_ids[] both appear canonical across HITL docs, breaking blocked-action parity.
Graph and evidence schemas remain run/node/tier-scoped without seam/package/lane/promotion/account lineage or contamination/safe-point provenance.
Executor_Protocol, Progression_Gates, and Run_Graph_View must reconcile lexicographic dispatch, scored scheduler, blocked overlays, and graph-local retry families into one lifecycle model.
